Brand guidelines · v1 · October 2026

People move
work forward.

Nordic Futurism: warm people, luminous threads.

The idea

01 · CONCEPT

GRTA is about people finding each other. The brand keeps people and relationships in front, and shows the technology only as the connections between them.

Warm people

Tactile, calm, real. Natural materials, daylight, generous space. The first thing you notice is always a person.

Luminous threads

Our futurism is quiet: fine fjord-blue lines and nodes that link people. They are how we draw Collective Intelligence.

Nordic clarity

Few colours, short sentences, lots of white space. Nothing shouts. Trust comes from calm.

Brand attributes
Human·Connected·Calm·Clear·Quietly ahead
AI + BI + CI = DI

Artificial Intelligence and Business Intelligence are only half the picture. Add the Collective Intelligence of your people and you get Decision Intelligence: better decisions, made faster, by the right people.

The GR/TA mark

02 · LOGO

Four letters, two by two, on one block. A redraw of the original GRTA mark: geometric letters on an even grid, so it stays crisp from a 1024 px app icon down to a 32 px favicon.

  • Primary: Ember letters on an Ink block. Use wherever possible.
  • Lockup: mark + “grta.ai” for headers and documents.
  • Mono: one colour on photos, partner materials and embossing.
  • Living mark: a thread of light traces the gutters between the letters. Loader and hero intro only.
  • Clear space: at least one letter cell (a third of the mark) on every side.
  • Minimum size: 24 px on screen, 8 mm in print. Below that, use the favicon render.

Colour

03 · COLOUR

A warm paper base, forest green for the brand, and ember used like a spice: the logo letters plus at most one accent per screen.

Voice & first components

08 · VOICE · UI
  • Human: “Find the people who can help.” Not “Leverage human capital.”
  • Clear: one idea per sentence. No em dashes.
  • Calm: confident, never hype. No exclamation marks.
  • Honest about AI: “GRTA suggests. You decide.”
  • Concrete: a real example beats an adjective.

“This one may look unusual. Here's why we think Lars could help.”
